title: Conceptual, Logical, and Physical Data Models
description: Trace one retailer relationship through conceptual, logical and physical models and see what each layer adds.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Knowledge Graph Applications and Data Architecture
chapter_title: Knowledge Graph Applications and Data Architecture

educational.learningObjective: Given a single business relationship, the learner will trace how it is represented differently at the conceptual, logical, and physical modeling layers, and explain what new detail each layer adds.
prerequisites: Has seen a database table or a graph node
Knows what a business relationship is
learningOutcomes: Trace one relationship across all three modeling layers
Explain why keeping the layers separate is worth the effort
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Give learners a business relationship and ask for all three representations, checking that no technology appears above the physical layer.

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Click-to-explain layered diagram with one running example
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Progressive specification of a single fixed example
pedagogical.feedbackType: A definition plus the same example re-expressed at each layer
misconceptionsAddressed: That the conceptual model is a rough draft of the physical one
That choosing a database is a modeling decision rather than an implementation one
discussionQuestions: Why do so many projects start at the physical layer and skip the other two?
What is lost when the conceptual model exists only in someone's head?
Does the graph implementation change the logical model, or only the physical one?
